prompt: The number of goals $X$ a soccer team scores in a match has distribution $P(0) = 0.3$, $P(1) = 0.4$, $P(2) = 0.3$. Find the variance $\sigma_X^2$. Round to the nearest tenth.
hint: Variance measures the average squared distance from the mean, so the mean has to be found before anything else.

hints.text: Variance measures the average squared distance from the mean, so the mean has to be found before anything else.
The mean is $0(0.3) + 1(0.4) + 2(0.3) = 1$. Square each value's distance from $1$, multiply by its probability, and add.

explanation: Start with the mean, since variance is measured around it: $\mu = 0(0.3) + 1(0.4) + 2(0.3) = 1$ goal.
Weight each squared distance from the mean by its probability: $(0-1)^2(0.3) = 0.3$, $(1-1)^2(0.4) = 0$ and $(2-1)^2(0.3) = 0.3$.
The sum is the variance, $\sigma_X^2 = 0.6$. (The standard deviation would be $\sqrt{0.6} \approx 0.77$ goals.)

alternativeExplanations.title: Use symmetry
steps: The distribution is symmetric around $1$ (0.3 on each side), so the mean is exactly $1$ with no arithmetic.
Only $X = 0$ and $X = 2$ are away from the mean, each 1 unit away, each with probability $0.3$.
